স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১) Most common cause of angina pectoris
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The most common cause of angina pectoris is atherosclerotic narrowing of the coronary arteries.

Mechanism:

  • Atherosclerotic plaques develop in coronary arteries → fixed narrowing of coronary lumen.

  • During increased myocardial oxygen demand (exercise, stress), the narrowed vessels cannot supply enough oxygen → myocardial ischaemia → angina pain.

Other options:

  • Thrombosis: Causes acute coronary syndromes (e.g., myocardial infarction) but is not the usual cause of stable angina.

  • Hyperlipidaemia: A major risk factor for atherosclerosis, not the direct cause.

  • Hypertension (HTN): A risk factor for coronary artery disease but not the most common direct cause.

Exam Pearl:
Commonest cause of angina pectoris → Coronary atherosclerosis.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ২) Vessels used in coronary artery bypass grafting except
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The brachial artery is not used as a conduit in coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG).

Common vessels used for CABG:

  • Internal mammary (internal thoracic) artery ✅

    • Most commonly used; especially left internal mammary artery (LIMA) to LAD due to excellent long-term patency.

  • Radial artery ✅

    • Common arterial graft, especially for coronary targets with significant stenosis.

  • Saphenous vein graft ✅

    • Most commonly used venous graft.

Brachial artery is not used because it is a major upper limb artery supplying the arm and is not suitable as a routine graft source.

Exam Pearl:
CABG grafts → Internal mammary artery + Radial artery + Saphenous vein.
Not used → Brachial artery.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ৩) The earliest change in ECG of MI is
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The earliest ECG change in acute myocardial infarction (MI) is usually ST segment deviation (especially ST elevation in STEMI).

Sequence of ECG changes in MI:

  1. Hyperacute T waves (earliest electrical change, may be transient)

  2. ST segment elevation/deviation (early diagnostic change) ✅

  3. T wave inversion (hours to days)

  4. Pathological Q waves (hours to days; indicate myocardial necrosis)

  5. T wave normalization (later)

Options:

  • T inversion: Occurs later during ischaemia/evolution of MI.

  • Pathological Q wave: Indicates established infarction, not the earliest change.

  • Widening of QRS: Not a typical early MI change.

Exam Pearl:
Earliest important ECG change in acute MI → ST segment elevation/deviation.
(Hyperacute T wave is the very first transient change, but among given options: ST deviation.)

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ৪) Pathognomonic for acute rheumatic fever
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The pathognomonic histological finding of acute rheumatic fever (ARF) is Aschoff nodules (Aschoff bodies).

Features of Aschoff nodules:

  • Found in the myocardium during rheumatic carditis

  • Consist of:

    • Central area of fibrinoid necrosis

    • Activated macrophages (Anitschkow cells / caterpillar cells)

    • Lymphocytes and plasma cells

Other options:

  • Pericarditis: May occur as part of pancarditis, but it is not pathognomonic.

  • Pancarditis: Classic cardiac manifestation of ARF involving endocardium, myocardium, and pericardium, but not diagnostic.

  • Fibrinoid degeneration: A feature of inflammatory/immune-mediated injury but not specific for ARF.

Exam Pearl:
Acute rheumatic fever → Aschoff bodies (nodules) = pathognomonic histological lesion.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ৫) Minor manifestation of rheumatic fever
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
In acute rheumatic fever (ARF), arthralgia is a minor manifestation according to the Jones criteria.

Jones Criteria:

Major manifestations:

  • Carditis ✅

  • Migratory polyarthritis

  • Sydenham chorea ✅

  • Erythema marginatum ✅

  • Subcutaneous nodules

Minor manifestations:

  • Arthralgia ✅

  • Fever

  • Raised inflammatory markers (ESR/CRP)

  • Prolonged PR interval on ECG

Why others are incorrect:

  • Carditis: Major manifestation.

  • Chorea: Major manifestation (Sydenham chorea).

  • Erythema marginatum: Major manifestation.

Exam Pearl:
Rheumatic fever minor criteria → Arthralgia, fever, raised ESR/CRP, prolonged PR interval.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ৬) The dominant symptom of MS
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The dominant symptom of Mitral stenosis (MS) is effort-related dyspnoea.

Mechanism:

  • Mitral valve narrowing causes obstruction of blood flow from the left atrium to the left ventricle.

  • This leads to:

    • Increased left atrial pressure

    • Pulmonary venous congestion

    • Pulmonary oedema → breathlessness, especially during exertion

Other symptoms of MS:

  • Orthopnoea

  • Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea

  • Fatigue

  • Palpitations (due to atrial fibrillation)

Options:

  • Chest pain: Not a dominant feature of MS.

  • Cough: May occur due to pulmonary congestion but is not the main symptom.

  • Palpitation: Common if atrial fibrillation develops, but less dominant.

Exam Pearl:
Mitral stenosis → Most common symptom = Exertional dyspnoea.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ৭) Austin Flint murmur is found in
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
Austin Flint murmur is a mid-diastolic rumbling murmur heard in severe aortic regurgitation (AR).

Mechanism:

  • In aortic regurgitation, blood flows back from the aorta into the left ventricle during diastole.

  • The regurgitant jet strikes the anterior mitral valve leaflet, causing it to partially close.

  • This produces a functional mitral stenosis-like effect → mid-diastolic rumbling murmur (Austin Flint murmur).

Options:

  • MS (Mitral stenosis): Causes a true mid-diastolic rumbling murmur with opening snap.

  • MR (Mitral regurgitation): Causes a pansystolic murmur.

  • TR (Tricuspid regurgitation): Causes a pansystolic murmur, louder on inspiration.

Exam Pearl:
Austin Flint murmur → Severe Aortic Regurgitation (AR).

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ৮) Most common cause of acute infective endocarditis
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The most common cause of acute infective endocarditis (IE) is Staphylococcus aureus.

Features of S. aureus endocarditis:

  • Causes acute, rapidly progressive endocarditis

  • Commonly affects:

    • Normal valves

    • Prosthetic valves (especially early after surgery)

    • IV drug users

  • Produces aggressive valve destruction and systemic infection

Other options:

  • Viridans streptococci: Most common cause of subacute infective endocarditis, especially on previously damaged valves.

  • Streptococcus gallolyticus (bovis): Associated with colorectal carcinoma and endocarditis.

  • Enterococci: Cause endocarditis, especially in older adults or after genitourinary procedures, but less common.

Exam Pearl:
Acute infective endocarditis → Staphylococcus aureus.
Subacute infective endocarditis → Viridans streptococci.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ৯) Pivotal investigation in infective endocarditis
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The pivotal investigation in infective endocarditis (IE) is echocardiography because it detects the key structural abnormality — vegetations on heart valves.

Role of echocardiography:

  • Demonstrates:

    • Vegetations

    • Valve destruction

    • Regurgitation

    • Abscess formation

  • Helps assess severity and complications

Types:

  • Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE): Initial test

  • Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE): More sensitive, especially for prosthetic valves or suspected complications

Other options:

  • Blood culture: Essential for identifying the causative organism and guiding antibiotic therapy, but does not demonstrate valve involvement.

  • ECG: May show conduction abnormalities but is not diagnostic.

  • CXR: May show complications like heart failure but is not diagnostic.

Exam Pearl:
Pivotal investigation in infective endocarditis → Echocardiography (TEE is more sensitive).

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১০) HTN with radiofemoral delay indicates
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
Hypertension with radiofemoral delay is a classic sign of coarctation of the aorta.

Mechanism:

  • Coarctation causes narrowing of the aorta, usually near the origin of the left subclavian artery (juxtaductal region).

  • This leads to:

    • High blood pressure in upper limbs

    • Delayed and weak femoral pulses

    • Radiofemoral delay (radial pulse occurs before femoral pulse)

Other features:

  • Systolic murmur over the back/interscapular region

  • Upper limb hypertension with lower limb hypotension

  • Rib notching on CXR due to collateral vessels

Options:

  • Pregnancy: Can cause hypertension but not radiofemoral delay.

  • Renal artery stenosis: Causes secondary hypertension but pulses remain normal.

  • Polycystic kidney disease: Can cause hypertension but not radiofemoral delay.

Exam Pearl:
Radiofemoral delay + hypertension → Coarctation of the aorta.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১১) Drug of choice in isolated systolic hypertension
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The drug of choice in isolated systolic hypertension (ISH), especially in elderly patients, is a calcium channel blocker (CCB) (particularly a dihydropyridine CCB like amlodipine).

Mechanism:

  • ISH occurs mainly due to reduced arterial compliance and increased arterial stiffness with aging.

  • CCBs reduce peripheral vascular resistance and effectively lower systolic blood pressure.

Other options:

  • ACE inhibitors: Useful in hypertension, especially with diabetes, CKD, or heart failure, but not first choice for ISH.

  • ARBs: Similar indications to ACE inhibitors; not preferred for isolated systolic hypertension.

  • Beta blockers: Less effective for ISH and generally not first-line unless there is another indication (e.g., angina, post-MI).

Exam Pearl:
Isolated systolic hypertension in elderly → Calcium channel blocker (e.g., amlodipine).

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১২) Antihypertensive contraindicated in gout
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
Thiazide diuretics are contraindicated or should be avoided in patients with gout because they can increase serum uric acid levels and precipitate gout attacks.

Mechanism:

  • Thiazides reduce uric acid excretion by the kidney → hyperuricaemia → gout flare.

Examples:

  • Hydrochlorothiazide

  • Chlorthalidone

Other options:

  • ARB: Most ARBs are neutral, but losartan is unique because it has a uricosuric effect and may be beneficial in gout.

  • CCB: Generally safe in gout.

  • Beta blockers: Not contraindicated, though not first-line in uncomplicated hypertension.

Exam Pearl:
Gout + Hypertension → Avoid thiazide diuretics.
Losartan is the preferred ARB in gout due to uric acid–lowering effect.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১৩) Drugs used in accelerated hypertension except
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
In accelerated (malignant) hypertension, the goal is controlled reduction of blood pressure using intravenous antihypertensive agents.

Commonly used drugs:

  • Labetalol ✅

    • IV α₁ + β blocker; commonly used in hypertensive emergencies.

  • GTN (Glyceryl trinitrate) ✅

    • IV vasodilator, especially useful when associated with myocardial ischaemia or heart failure.

  • Hydralazine ✅

    • Direct arteriolar vasodilator; used particularly in pregnancy-related hypertensive emergencies.

Frusemide (Furosemide) ❌

  • It is a loop diuretic used mainly for fluid overload and pulmonary oedema.

  • It is not a primary antihypertensive agent for accelerated hypertension.

Exam Pearl:
Hypertensive emergency drugs → Labetalol, GTN, Hydralazine, Sodium nitroprusside.
Frusemide is used only when volume overload is present.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১৪) Not a Pathognomonic feature of VT
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
Extreme left axis deviation (LAD) is not a pathognomonic feature of ventricular tachycardia (VT).

Features strongly suggestive/pathognomonic of VT on ECG include:

  • AV dissociation 

    • Atria and ventricles depolarize independently.

  • Capture beats 

    • A normal supraventricular impulse briefly captures the ventricles.

  • Fusion beats 

    • Combination of a normal conducted beat and a ventricular beat.

Why others are incorrect:

  • Capture beats: Highly suggestive of VT.

  • Fusion beats: Highly suggestive of VT.

  • AV dissociation: A classic diagnostic feature of VT.

Extreme LAD may occur in VT but can also be seen in other conditions (e.g., conduction abnormalities, ventricular pacing, structural heart disease), so it is not specific.

Exam Pearl:
VT diagnostic clues → AV dissociation + capture beats + fusion beats.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১৫) Altered colour vision is associated with toxicity of
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
Altered colour vision (especially yellow vision or xanthopsia) is a classic sign of digoxin toxicity.

Mechanism:

  • Digoxin toxicity affects retinal and visual pathways.

  • It can cause:

    • Yellow/green vision (xanthopsia)

    • Blurred vision

    • Visual disturbances

Other features of digoxin toxicity:

  • Nausea, vomiting

  • Confusion

  • Cardiac arrhythmias (especially AV block and ventricular arrhythmias)

Other options:

  • GTN: Causes headache, flushing, hypotension; not colour vision changes.

  • Amiodarone: Can cause corneal deposits and optic neuropathy, but altered colour vision is not the classic exam association.

  • Verapamil: Causes bradycardia, constipation, and AV block; not colour changes.

Exam Pearl:
Digoxin toxicity → Yellow vision (xanthopsia) + arrhythmias.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১৬) Mechanism of heart failure following MI
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The main mechanism of heart failure following myocardial infarction (MI) is reduced ventricular contractility due to loss of functioning myocardium.

Mechanism:

  • MI causes myocardial necrosis due to coronary artery occlusion.

  • Damaged ventricular muscle cannot contract effectively → reduced systolic function.

  • This leads to:

    • ↓ Cardiac output

    • ↑ Ventricular filling pressures

    • Pulmonary congestion → heart failure symptoms

Other options:

  • Ventricular outflow obstruction: Seen in conditions like hypertrophic cardiomyopathy or valvular stenosis, not typical after MI.

  • Ventricular inflow obstruction: Seen in mitral/tricuspid valve obstruction.

  • Ventricular volume overload: Occurs in valvular regurgitation or shunts.

Exam Pearl:
Heart failure after MI → Loss of myocardium → ↓ ventricular contractility → ↓ cardiac output.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১৭) ST elevation with upward concavity & PR interval depression in ECG suggests
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The ECG features of acute pericarditis are:

  • Diffuse ST segment elevation with upward concavity ✅

  • PR interval depression ✅ (classic finding)

Mechanism:

  • Inflammation of the pericardium causes widespread subepicardial injury currents, producing diffuse ST elevation.

  • Atrial involvement causes PR segment depression.

ECG stages of acute pericarditis:

  1. Diffuse ST elevation + PR depression

  2. ST segments return to baseline

  3. T-wave inversion

  4. ECG normalization

Other options:

  • Cardiac tamponade: May occur as a complication of pericarditis but does not produce this typical ECG pattern.

  • Acute myocarditis: May show nonspecific ST-T changes but not classic PR depression.

  • Infective endocarditis: Usually causes no characteristic ST elevation pattern.

Exam Pearl:
Diffuse concave ST elevation + PR depression → Acute pericarditis.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১৮) Definitive investigation for pericardial effusion
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The definitive investigation for pericardial effusion is echocardiography.

Why echocardiography:

  • It directly visualizes fluid collection in the pericardial space.

  • It can assess:

    • Amount of effusion

    • Cardiac chamber compression

    • Signs of cardiac tamponade (e.g., right atrial/right ventricular collapse)

    • Haemodynamic effect

Other options:

  • ECG: May show low voltage QRS and electrical alternans in large effusions, but it is not diagnostic.

  • Blood culture: Used only when infection is suspected, not for detecting effusion.

  • CXR: May show "water bottle" heart in large effusions but is not definitive.

Exam Pearl:
Pericardial effusion → Definitive test = Echocardiography.

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ১৯) Most common congenital cardiac malformation
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
The most common congenital cardiac malformation is Ventricular Septal Defect (VSD).

Mechanism:

  • VSD is a defect in the interventricular septum causing communication between the left and right ventricles.

  • It usually produces a left-to-right shunt after birth due to higher left ventricular pressure.

  • Large VSDs can lead to:

    • Heart failure

    • Pulmonary hypertension

    • Eisenmenger syndrome (if untreated)

Other options:

  • ASD: Common congenital heart defect but less common than VSD.

  • PDA: Common in premature infants but not the most common overall.

  • TOF: Most common cyanotic congenital heart disease, not the most common congenital cardiac defect.

Exam Pearl:
Most common congenital heart disease → VSD.
Most common cyanotic congenital heart disease → Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF).

স্পেশাল কুইজ.question: ২০) A continuous machinery murmur is found in
স্পেশাল কুইজ.exp:
A continuous machinery murmur is the classic murmur of Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA).

Mechanism:

  • PDA is a persistent connection between the descending aorta and pulmonary artery.

  • Because aortic pressure remains higher than pulmonary artery pressure during both systole and diastole, blood flows continuously through the ductus.

  • This produces a continuous “machinery-like” murmur, best heard at the left upper sternal border/infraclavicular area.

Other options:

  • ASD: Causes a systolic ejection murmur with fixed wide splitting of S2.

  • VSD: Causes a harsh pansystolic murmur.

  • TOF: Causes a systolic ejection murmur due to right ventricular outflow obstruction.

Exam Pearl:
Continuous machinery murmur → PDA.
VSD → pansystolic murmur; ASD → fixed split S2; TOF → ejection systolic murmur.
